items.title: Kinetic modelling of Chlorella spp. wastewater treatment and resource recovery in the food industry
items.abstract: Abstract Effluents generated in the food and beverage industry typically contain elevated concentrations of organic carbon sources and inorganic nutrients, representing a significant environmental burden as global food demand continues to rise. Owing to their capacity to effectively assimilate carbon and nutrients while simultaneously generating biomass with potential valorization pathways, Chlorella spp. offers a dual benefit of contaminant removal and resource recovery. However, existing algal studies remain predominantly at the laboratory scale, and their competitive advantages have not been demonstrated for full-scale implementation. Kinetic modelling represents an essential tool to elucidate algal growth behavior, optimize operational conditions, and predict performance of algal systems for accurate scale-up, but limited studies are available to comprehensively review kinetic models of Chlorella spp. In this review, kinetic models were synthesized, including sigmoidal growth models (Gompertz, logistic, and Verhulst), single-factor and inhibition models (Monod and Andrews), light-dependent photobioreactor models (Huisman), multifactor and interaction models for co-cultures (Lotka–Volterra). Kinetic parameters from these models were compiled to support consistent projections from lab-scale to industrial-scale systems, enabling future techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessment of algal systems. Other emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence and machine learning approaches, were also reviewed. The review also identified benchmark processes and outlined a decision tree for developing strategies to enhance resource recovery and phycoremediation performance. Finally, key research needs have been highlighted to guide future work in the field.

items.title: KoAGE: Do Large Language Models Know, Learn, and Coin Korean Neologisms?
items.abstract: Korean neologisms arise through diverse mechanisms, a demanding test of language models beyond lexical memorization. To enable systematic evaluation, we introduce NeoTrace, an automated, rerunnable framework that collects and dates neologisms across genres. Its 4,271 entries support KoAGE, a cutoff-aware benchmark with three acquisition and two generation tasks---the latter, to our knowledge, the first to compare model coinages with attested neologisms under their original materials and community context. Across 21 models, lexical recall diverges from contextual inference: in a five-model temporal analysis, models define only 13-30% of cutoff-year words, yet can infer meaning from one usage. However, structural understanding remains limited: even correct definitions barely improve formation analysis of pre-cutoff neologisms. Given word-building materials, single models often follow human formation mechanisms, whereas multi-agent coinage favors abbreviation and depends on interaction framing. items.title: L'intégration didactique des outils de l'intelligence artificielle générative dans l'enseignement secondaire et supérieur au Maroc : Enjeux, pratiques et modélisation systémique
items.abstract: Résumé :Le présent article se propose d’examiner l'intégration didactique des technologies d'intelligence artificielle générative (IAG) au sein des établissements d'enseignement secondaire et supérieur au Maroc. Face à la mutation rapide des écosystèmes pédagogiques mondiaux et nationaux, force est de constater que l'émergence des agents conversationnels et des modèles linguistiques transforme profondément les processus d'enseignement-apprentissage, l'ingénierie des manuels scolaires et les modalités d'évaluation. S'appuyant sur un cadre théorique multidisciplinaire combinant la théorie socioconstructiviste, la théorie de la charge cognitive (Sweller) et les modèle TPACK (Mishra & Koehler), cet article formule un modèle didactique conceptuel d'ingénierie intégrée. À partir d'une méthodologie mixte combinant des observations empiriques, une analyse textuelle didactique et des enquêtes quantitatives auprès de 320 enseignants et étudiants de la région de l'Oriental, nous évaluons le niveau d'appropriation de l'IAG, la perception des compétences d'escorte pédagogique ainsi que les risques de fracture numérique et d'altération de la réflexivité. Les résultats révèlent une adhésion forte mais non structurée (74 % d'usage informel), marquée par une faible littératie IA critique et un manque d'alignement institutionnel. Nous proposons enfin des recommandations stratégiques axées sur l'éthique, la formation continue et l'innovation numérique pérenne. Mots-clés : Intelligence Artificielle Générative, Didactique, Innovation Pédagogique, Manuels Scolaires, Université Mohammed Premier, ingénierie de formation. Abstract:This prospective and analytical study examines the didactic integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) tools in secondary and higher education institutions in Morocco. In light of the rapid transformation of global and national educational ecosystems, the emergence of conversational agents and large language models is fundamentally altering teaching-learning processes, textbook engineering, and assessment frameworks. Grounded in a multidisciplinary theoretical framework combining socio-constructivist theory, Cognitive Load Theory (Sweller), and the TPACK model (Mishra & Koehler), this paper formulates a conceptual didactic model of integrated engineering. Utilizing a mixed-methods approach that includes empirical observations, didactic textual analysis, and quantitative surveys among 320 educators and students in the Oriental region, we evaluate the level of GAI adoption, pedagogical scaffolding competencies, and the risks of digital divide and critical reflexivity decline. Findings indicate high yet unstructured adoption (74% informal usage), characterized by limited critical AI literacy and institutional misalignment. Strategic recommendations emphasizing ethical governance, continuous professional development, and sustainable digital innovation are provided. items.title: L2G-SR: Learning to Guide LLM-based Symbolic Regression
items.abstract: Symbolic regression searches for an equation that explains observed data. Numerical error is commonly used to guide the search, but it alone can favor an accurate surrogate over a candidate with the right structure. We propose L2G-SR, a framework for LLM-based symbolic regression that guides search with a learned structural verifier. We construct structural supervision signal using tree edit distance (TED), accounting for commutative operators and alternative expression forms. A verifier first aligns numerical observations with the formulas, then learns to score a candidate's structural similarity to the target formula. At search time, the target formula is hidden and the verifier complements numerical error in parent selection. An analyst then uses verifier feedback and diagnostic tools to propose revisions, which a generator converts into refined expressions. On LLM-SRBench, L2G-SR achieves state-of-the-art numerical fit, equation level accuracy and TED across the evaluated LLM backbones and domains. L2G-SR demonstrates the value of learned structural guidance for LLM-based symbolic regression.

items.title: La Ley Silla en México: análisis de sus implicaciones legales, empresariales y de salud ocupacional
items.abstract: The "Chair Law" (Ley Silla) is a reform to Mexico's Federal Labor Law that guarantees workers the right to rest periods when their duties require them to remain standing for extended periods during the workday. Its legal foundation is established in Article 123 of the Political Constitution of the United Mexican States, the Federal Labor Law, and the Official Mexican Standards governing ergonomics, occupational safety, and health. The corresponding provisions came fully into force on December 15, 2025. Scientific evidence strongly supports this measure, demonstrating that prolonged standing increases the risk of venous insufficiency, lower back and neck pain, muscle fatigue, and chronic musculoskeletal disorders. Consequently, alternating between standing and sitting is widely recommended as a key preventive ergonomic strategy. Although some business sectors have expressed concerns regarding implementation costs and workplace adaptations, the long-term benefits of improved occupational health, including reduced absenteeism, lower staff turnover, and decreased medical expenses, are expected to outweigh the initial investment. Overall, this reform represents a significant step toward protecting workers' health, promoting decent working conditions, and strengthening labor rights. Nevertheless, its effectiveness will ultimately depend on adequate enforcement, monitoring, and compliance.

items.title: LabCompiler: A Framework for Verifiable Human-Machine Laboratory Execution from Imperfect Protocols
items.abstract: Closing the loop of AI-driven science requires reliably translating natural-language protocols into executable laboratory workflows despite protocol defects and heterogeneous hardware. Existing approaches often couple scientific interpretation with device-specific code generation, making errors difficult to localize and limiting reuse across laboratory platforms. We introduce LabCompiler, a robust protocol-to-execution framework that transforms imperfect natural-language protocols into verifiable human-machine workflows. Its protocol firewall diagnoses and repairs defects before compilation while preserving unaffected content, guided by troubleshooting knowledge accumulated through perturbation-guided self-evolution. A two-level, device-agnostic graph representation separates experimental semantics from hardware-specific implementation and supports capability-based device assignment with coordinated human execution. We further introduce a protocol recovery benchmark covering four controlled perturbation types and naturally occurring errors collected from protocols written by iGEM participants. Experiments show that LabCompiler outperforms frontier LLMs in protocol error correction while enabling coordinated human-machine execution across heterogeneous, partially automated laboratory settings.

items.title: Large Language Model–Assisted Qualitative Analysis: A Case Study of Medical Students with Academic Difficulties
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support qualitative research, yet practical accounts of how they can be incorporated without displacing human interpretation remain limited. This study presents a researcher-supervised workflow for processing and analysing semi-structured interviews with medical students experiencing academic difficulties. Thirty interviews were transcribed, checked against recordings, de-identified, and analysed through three stages: event/theme identification, element-level examination of focal events, and cross-event interpretive construction. The workflow identified recurring difficulties involving unclear learning goals, limited learning resources, professional-identity tension, and family expectations. LLMs supported the organisation of long transcripts and the comparison of related experiences; researchers verified outputs, retained contextual qualifications, and developed the final interpretation. The findings illustrate that LLMs can make qualitative analysis more traceable and efficient when their outputs are treated as provisional analytic material rather than authoritative conclusions. We propose practical safeguards for transcription, privacy, validation, and documentation. This case study offers a concise, reproducible pathway for using LLMs to assist—not replace—qualitative inquiry.

items.title: LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS FOR SERVICE-ORIENTED COMPUTING: A CASE STUDY IN TELECOM CUSTOMER SUPPORT SYSTEMS
items.abstract: Increasingly complex telecommunications systems demand the application of intelligent and efficient methods to ensure smooth operations, sound decision-making and high-level services. With the increasing paradigm of Service-Oriented Computing (SOC) - where systems are composed of distributed services, the management of such services is becoming an even greater challenge in the customer support domain. One of the key obstacles in customer support is obtaining real time diagnostics of the problem and creating a detailed report that confirms the occurrence of the failure. This paper explores the functions and potential provided by large language models in the context of telecom customer support. The paper particularly explores the opportunities provided for automatic summarization of interactions, artificial intelligence in knowledge management and enhancement of the service diagnostics functionalities. The research is carried out through a case study, analyzing existing solutions applied in practical scenarios such as diagnostic platforms, CRM systems and AI assistants. The study explored human-in-the-loop approaches of agent feedback, which trains the AI to improve its output for better accuracy, adaptability and overall reliability. The findings revealed that Large Language Models (LLMs) boosted agent productivity, reduced human work and ensured consistency in communication. However, the output of the LLMs also presented some issues including inaccuracies and data privacy. Based on the study’s results, Large Language Models (LLMs) are actually used as a complement to human agents, enabling building more intelligent, adaptable and efficient service-oriented telecom systems.

items.title: LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS IN SEPSIS WITH HALLUCINATIONS: NARRATIVE REVIEW AND ANALYSIS OF TEN CASES
items.abstract: Objectives. Large language models (LLMs) are advancing rapidly in emergency and critical care, but the generation of “hallucinations” - unverifiable statements that contradict guidelines or extrapolate without support — remains a major patient-safety risk. Building on our previous work in Arta Medica (2024) and Healthcare Informatics Research (2026), this study characterises the prevalence, typology and potential impact of hallucinations produced by a medical LLM (Palmyra-Med 70B) in early sepsis management, based on an index case and a cohort of ten clinical vignettes. Material and Methods. Ten sepsis vignettes (eight from the open MIMIC-IV-demo database and two from the literature) were submitted to a software application based on the Palmyra-Med 70B LLM, embedded in a retrieval-augmented multi-agent system. The generated recommendations (management, antibiotics, guideline compliance with the Surviving Sepsis Campaign) were assessed independently by two ICU physicians using a standardised form; hallucinations were operationally defined and flagged by consensus. Results. The LLM produced recommendations of medium-to-high relevance and grounding (mostly 7–10/10 across both raters). Hallucinations were identified in 3 of 10 cases (Cases 1, 9 and 10), all involving the fabrication or unjustified extrapolation of clinical signs/values absent from the vignette (altered mental status, hyperlactatemia, hyperglycemia, septic shock). Non-hallucinating cases (2–8) still showed minor divergences from the guidelines, expressed as suboptimal compliance scores. Conclusions. Palmyra-Med 70B can provide useful support in the early phase of sepsis management, but requires active clinical oversight and a hybrid clinician-LLM workflow to limit hallucinations and safeguard patient safety.

items.title: Latent profiles of academic stress and exercise motivation among college students: A latent profile analysis
items.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the latent profile structure of academic stress and exercise motivation among Chinese college students and to examine the predictive effects of demographic variables, including gender, body mass index (BMI), grade, and household registration background, on profile membership. From May 14 to June 3, 2025, convenience cluster sampling was employed to recruit 1,346 first- to third-year undergraduate students. The participants completed the Academic Sub-Scale and the Chinese-translated Behavioral Regulation in Exercise Questionnaire-2. Latent profile analysis was performed using Mplus 8.3 to identify distinct combined patterns of academic stress and exercise motivation, and the R3STEP method was applied to test the predictive utility of demographic variables on profile assignment. Four latent profiles were identified as the best-fitting solution. Profile 1, the High stress-low motivation profile (9.0%), was characterized by elevated academic stress and low scores across all exercise motivation dimensions. Profile 2, the High stress-high motivation profile (7.4%), exhibited the highest academic stress and the highest levels of external, introjected, and identified regulation. Profile 3, the Low stress-high autonomy profile (22.1%), demonstrated the lowest academic stress and the highest intrinsic motivation. Profile 4, the Moderate-balanced adaptation profile (61.6%), was marked by moderate scores on all variables and represented the most prevalent pattern. items.title: Learning by Examples: Power Grid Steady State Analysis with a Tabular Foundation Model
items.abstract: Foundation models have shown strong generalization across scientific domains, but their use in power systems remains largely task-specific. We investigate whether a pretrained tabular foundation model (TFM), TabPFN, can serve as a general-purpose neural solver for power grid steady-state analysis. We evaluate the TFM on three tasks: power flow (PF) prediction, N-k contingency screening (NCS), and voltage stability margin (VSM) prediction. We performed experiments on 118- and 2000-bus systems, comparing the TFM against task-specific neural baselines. Without retraining or fine-tuning, the TFM matches or outperforms the best task-specific model in several settings across the three tasks. For 118-bus PF prediction, a variant of the TFM achieves errors of $1\times 10^{-3}$ pu for voltage magnitudes and $0.30^\circ$ for voltage angles, outperforming all baselines. On unseen N-1 contingency and close-to-infeasible PF cases, the TFM is competitive with the DCPF approximation. For millions of unseen N-2 contingencies, the TFM achieves AUCs of 0.92 and 0.95 for branch and voltage violation screening, respectively. The TFM also attains accurate VSM prediction performance for the 2000-bus system with limited labelled data. The TFM attains strong results across the tested tasks despite pretraining without any power-system-specific dataset and requiring no fine-tuning step. These results offer a glimpse into the potential of pretrained TFMs as a neural solver for a range of power grid analysis tasks.

items.title: Learning Perception to Action Rules through Reinforcement Learning for Theory-of-Mind Reasoning
items.abstract: In Theory-of-Mind (ToM) reasoning, large language models may correctly infer the agent's mental state but fail to use that inference when predicting or judging the agent's subsequent actions. In this work, we investigate whether explicitly connecting perception, belief, and action with rules improves ToM reasoning. We generate concise \textit{if--then} rules that express relations between perception to action and use Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to train Qwen2.5 and Llama3 models across four ToM benchmarks. GRPO with rule generation outperforms prompting, supervised fine-tuning, and think reasoning. Moreover, rules generated by larger models ($\geq$3B) provide transferable knowledge that improves downstream performance of GPT-4o-mini. These findings suggest that explicit rules help models bridge the reasoning gap in ToM and support knowledge transfer across models.

items.title: Learning Visual Speech Representations via Cross-Modal Distillation and Joint Face-Lip Modeling
items.abstract: Lipreading remains challenging due to the inherent ambiguity of visual speech cues and their sensitivity to head pose and video resolution. In this work, we propose FLARE, a framework for robust visual speech representation learning via cross-modal distillation and joint face-lip modeling. FLARE leverages semantically rich Whisper representations as the acoustic teacher signal, converting them into discrete distillation targets through a random-projection quantizer and pretraining the model with a masked prediction objective. To capture complementary visual information, FLARE employs a dual-stream architecture that jointly processes lip region-of-interest (ROI) and full-face inputs, where the lip stream captures finegrained articulatory motion and the face stream encodes broader facial dynamics. During pretraining, auxiliary audio input is incorporated to facilitate cross-modal alignment, and modality dropout is applied to encourage robust visual-only representations. For downstream lipreading, FLARE serves as a visual encoder coupled with either a lightweight Transformer decoder or an LLM-based decoder. Evaluated on LRS2, LRS3, and the out-of-domain WildVSR benchmark, FLARE achieves strong lipreading performance, with word error rates of 11.7%, 13.2%, and 34.3%, respectively. A progressive design study confirms the contribution of each major component. Further analyses demonstrate that joint face-lip modeling improves robustness under degraded video resolution and large head pose variation, while yielding more phoneme-discriminative visual representations. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/jxzhanggg/FLARE.

items.title: Learning What to Keep: Transfer-Aware Personal Skill Learning from User Feedback
items.abstract: User feedback enables LLMs to refine reusable personalized skills, but often mixes persistent preferences with request-specific corrections. Indiscriminately retaining both risks negative transfer, motivating selective retention at the level of individual requirements. We frame this challenge as selective transfer over atomic rules and propose SkillGrain, a framework for learning reusable personalized skills from user feedback. SkillGrain decomposes feedback into independently actionable rules, predicts their transferability, and retains only those suitable for future requests. To learn these decisions, we combine rubric-guided skill rewards with fine-grained credit assignment that separately evaluates rule content and retention decisions. We further jointly optimize skill induction and skill-conditioned generation through reinforcement learning, ensuring that learned skills support downstream personalization. We construct a benchmark spanning five personalized writing tasks to evaluate cross-request generalization. Experiments across three base models in both in-domain and out-of-domain settings show that SkillGrain achieves the best overall average performance among competing methods.

items.title: Learning When to Trust Medical Knowledge: Regression-Safe Routing for Clinical Reasoning
items.abstract: Clinical reasoning LLMs need external medical knowledge, but retrieved evidence and reasoning chains can be outdated, poisoned, or hallucinated. Harmful knowledge can cause regression: changing a correct answer into an incorrect one. We construct a medical knowledge-poisoning benchmark covering retrieved evidence and reasoning chains, with seven attack families filtered by a three-judge "subtle-but-wrong" vote and paired clean exams that separate poisoning effects from question difficulty. No fixed knowledge-use strategy is robust across these settings: strong RAG methods trade robustness to poisoned evidence against accuracy when evidence is useful. We formulate knowledge use as per-instance routing and introduce Med-TrustRouter, a lightweight controller that keeps the solver frozen. From leakage-free runtime signals, it estimates each action's expected correctness gain and uncertainty, preserving the base answer unless another action is confidently better. Across seven medical reasoning settings, Med-TrustRouter achieves 78.9 macro and 69.2 worst-case accuracy, matching the strongest competitor on macro accuracy while substantially improving the worst-case floor. Its gains transfer across solvers and evidence judges, unlike a hand-coded router using the same signals. Similar performance across linear, tree, and neural action-value heads suggests that the benefit comes from routing rather than estimator complexity. These results support learning when to trust external knowledge for robust clinical reasoning.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

items.title: Learning-enabled collaborative intelligence in search and rescue robotics: a survey of paradigms, models, and challenges
items.abstract: Search and Rescue (SAR) robotics increasingly depends on collaborative intelligence to operate effectively in dynamic, uncertain, and time-sensitive environments. Modern SAR missions require coordinated interaction among heterogeneous robotic agents as well as structured collaboration between humans and intelligent systems for perception, decision-making, and adaptive mission execution. This paper presents a structured narrative review supported by a systematic literature search of learning-enabled collaborative intelligence frameworks in SAR robotics, organized around three paradigms: human-to-machine (H2M), machine-to-machine (M2M), and machine-to-human (M2H) learning. The review examines recent developments in reinforcement learning, federated and decentralized learning, knowledge distillation, swarm intelligence, semantic communication, and the growing integration of large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) for knowledge grounding, transfer, and explainability. Beyond algorithmic advances, the analysis emphasizes deployment-oriented challenges including partial observability, communication constraints, uncertainty management, model reliability, and real-time operational requirements. Rather than conducting a fully PRISMA-compliant systematic review, this work synthesizes representative and influential studies to identify emerging trends, architectural trade-offs, deployment limitations, and future research directions for scalable and trustworthy collaborative SAR systems.

items.title: LEGAL CONFLICTS IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY: THE UKRAINIAN AND EUROPEAN EXPERIENCE
items.abstract: This article examines the ethical and legal issues arising in the digital economy. These conflicts are conceptualised as contradictions between innovative technological practices, ethical norms and applicable legislation. Three key types of conflict are identified: those relating to privacy and data monetisation, algorithmic autonomy and accountability, and digital security and fundamental rights. Particular emphasis is placed on the wartime context in Ukraine, which presents unique challenges for digital transformation and legal regulation. Methodology. The research methodology employed is a synthesis of the comparative legal method and a Law and Economics approach. The comparative legal method is employed to compare the regulatory instruments of the European Union (GDPR, AI Act, DSA, DMA) with those of Ukraine (the Laws of Ukraine ‘On Personal Data Protection’, ‘On Virtual Assets’, ‘On Media’, and ‘On Electronic Communications’). The empirical basis of the study comprises reports by the European Commission (Digital Economy and Society Index, DESI), Eurostat statistical data on the digital transformation of EU Member States, and analytical materials published by the OECD (Digital Economy Outlook) and the World Bank (Digital Development Report). The Law and Economics analysis is employed to evaluate the impact of legal conflicts on the investment climate, transaction costs and innovation activity. Results. The study demonstrates that the development of the digital economy in Ukraine and the European Union is determined not only by the pace of digital technology adoption, but also by the quality of the institutional environment in which digital markets operate. The European model is distinguished by the establishment of common rules governing data flows, the utilisation of artificial intelligence, and the operation of digital platforms. This contributes to a reduction in regulatory uncertainty for businesses and the creation of conditions conducive to long-term investment in digital technologies. Ukraine continues to face an institutional and technological gap with the EU, as evidenced by uneven levels of business digitalisation, limited investment capacity among some businesses in digital infrastructure, and heightened risks associated with the use of data and artificial intelligence technologies. At the same time, a lack of clear rules governing the digital economy could lead to higher transaction costs for businesses, reduce investment activity and make it more difficult for Ukrainian companies to access the European digital market. The study establishes that digital regulatory conflicts have not only legal but also direct economic effects: they affect regulatory compliance costs, the level of market competition, access to digital services, consumer trust, and the ability of businesses to scale digital business models. In this context, the harmonisation of Ukraine's digital environment with European approaches may be regarded as one of the factors reducing institutional barriers to digital investment and deepening Ukraine's economic integration with the EU. Practical Implications. The practical value of the findings lies in their potential application to shaping Ukraine's economic policy on digital transformation, aimed not merely at regulatory adaptation but, above all, at creating conditions to increase enterprise productivity, attract investment, and expand the participation of Ukrainian firms in European digital markets. Priority areas include reducing regulatory and transaction costs for digital businesses; establishing rules for data flows and AI deployment that align with the European market; promoting the digitalisation of small and medium-sized enterprises; developing digital infrastructure; and encouraging competition in digital markets. The implementation of these measures takes on additional economic significance under martial law, as digital technologies can ensure business continuity, reduce the costs of coordinating economic processes and boost enterprise resilience to external shocks. Therefore, the effectiveness of harmonisation with European digital regulations should be assessed not only by the number of provisions implemented, but also by their impact on investment activity, productivity, competitiveness and the resilience of Ukraine’s digital economy. Value / Originality. The scientific novelty of the study lies in its identification of the economic consequences of regulatory and ethico-legal conflicts arising during the digital transformation of Ukraine's economy and its integration into the European digital space. The proposed typology of key conflicts enables the systematisation of factors that generate regulatory uncertainty, increase transaction costs, and affect investment activity and the competitiveness of digital economy enterprises. The developed cyclical model of conflict evolution is intended as a tool for identifying the interrelationship between technological change, regulatory adaptation, economic costs, and institutional responses. Its application may prove useful in assessing the digital resilience of the economy, underpinning public policy on digital transformation, and setting priorities for Ukraine's economic integration into the European digital market amid wartime conditions and post-conflict recovery.

items.title: Let Me Clarify: Interactive Modeling of Soft Attributes
items.abstract: People commonly express preferences through soft attributes such as is interesting,'' which are difficult to operationalize for computational preference modeling. Latent representations can obscure how such attributes are interpreted, limiting transparency and user control. We formalize softness as the diversity of valid interpretations a description permits and provide empirical support for this characterization. Our proposed measure estimates softness to guide clarification and determine when to generate computational approximations. This is instantiated in AttriFy, a mixed-initiative system that translates descriptions into executable Python functions over text corpora. An interactive dashboard connects the dialogue to proposed functions and computed values, enabling users to inspect, accept, reject, and refine interpretations. An exploratory within-subjects study with 32 participants compares our softness-guided clarification approach with an LLM baseline in supporting interpretable attribute construction. This work positions softness as a basis for constructing explicit, user-steerable attribute dimensions for downstream preference elicitation and decision-making.

items.abstract: This chapter examines the role of educational technologies in facilitating effective online academic advising through a qualitative case study approach in a higher education institution. items.title: Lexical Persistence Without Semantic Entrenchment in AI Agent Communities
items.abstract: AI agent communities sustain lexical persistence, popular terms spread, recur, and achieve broad adoption, but whether they also develop the temporal semantic structure characteristic of human linguistic communities remains open. We compare MoltBook (AI agent community, 8 weeks), PTT (Chinese human BBS, 19 years), and Reddit (English human forum, in matched 8-week windows) using Compass-Aligned Distributional Embeddings (CADE), measuring semantic drift (B1), neighborhood stability (B2), and lag-1 autocorrelation of per-word drift trajectories. Across the platforms, lag-1 autocorrelation forms a memory-horizon continuum. AI agents' result clusters at the low end, while human platforms show longer-range temporal dependence. MoltBook exhibits approximately 2$\times$ the B1 drift and 20-30% lower B2 stability than both human platforms. As a partial control for community age, r/vibecoding (founded 2025-02-08) shows significant ACF in its first 8 weeks ($0.082$, $p<.001$) and over 15 weeks ($0.220$, $p<.001$); MoltBook's ACF remains non-significant ($p = 0.41$), consistent with the gap not reducing to developmental stage alone. We interpret this pattern as evidence that lexical diffusion alone does not guarantee diachronic semantic consolidation. The findings are consistent with a contrast between communities whose semantic trajectories accumulate long-range interaction constraints and communities whose outputs are repeatedly regenerated from largely fixed pretrained distributions.

items.title: Lightweight 3D Convolutional Networks for Biomechanical Motion Analysis in Martial Arts Training
items.abstract: To reduce the subjectivity of traditional martial arts training assessment and avoid the deployment requirements of wearable devices, the study develops an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted analysis system based on a 3D Convolutional Neural Network (3D CNN). This study adopts a 3D CNN as the backbone network and develops optimization strategies from four aspects. Spatiotemporal decomposition convolution factorizes standard 3D convolution kernels into a combination of spatial convolution and temporal convolution. The temporal attention mechanism adaptively computes the importance weight of each frame, enabling the model to focus on key action frames. A dynamic inference mechanism determines whether computation should be terminated early based on the confidence of intermediate-layer outputs, thereby reducing redundant computation. Knowledge distillation uses only the class-similarity soft distribution of a large teacher model to supervise the lightweight student model. This reduces the loss of feature representation caused by network compression and helps maintain recognition accuracy with fewer parameters. Experimental results are obtained on the Chain-of-Thought Action Form Assessment (CoT-AFA) and Martial Arts, Dancing and Sports Dataset (MADS) public datasets. The results show that the proposed method achieves a Top-1 accuracy of 74.2% on the CoT-AFA dataset, which is close to the 75.3% achieved by Video Swin Transformer. Meanwhile, the proposed method reduces the number of parameters by approximately 52.3% (14.2M vs. 29.8M) and decreases Floating Point Operations per Second by approximately 43.7% (52.4G vs. 93.0G). In addition, the mean squared error (MSE) for quality evaluation is reduced to 1.48. On the MADS dataset, the Top-1 accuracy reaches 68.9%, while the mean per-joint position error is reduced to 60.5 mm. The results support the use of the system for video-based analysis in martial arts training.

items.title: Likelihood Is Not Authorship: Can We Reliably Measure Human Contribution in AI-Assisted Writing?
items.abstract: AI-text detection generally asks whether a machine wrote a text. As AI becomes an increasingly integral and accepted part of writing, the more relevant question is no longer whether AI was used, but how much of the text reflects human contribution. A prominent line of work estimates this by measuring how predictive a person's prompt is of the final text. We show that this measure can be easily manipulated. We introduce SPECIFICITY PADDING that simply asks the model to copy a few random IDs from the prompt, and that alone makes a title-only request look more human than one that supplies the article's key ideas. A context-swap audit then holds each document fixed, and only shows or hides the IDs to the evaluator. The score of the unchanged text swings by a third to half of its scale, and it rises for every document we test, on news and scientific abstracts, across varied LLMs from 3.8B to 753B parameters. The same articles can average 85\% human or 15\% human depending only on which prompt is on record, and even with no prompt at all, the output-only variant rewards the random strings themselves. An exact identity, the credit ledger, explains why. The score is a surprisal-weighted average over the text, so rare strings that the context makes copyable collect the credit, whatever they mean. A two-point bound marks a deeper limit. If the prompt could have been machine-written, every transcript-only method must, in the worst case, miss by half the contribution at stake. Likelihood-based scores alone cannot reliably establish human contribution without evidence of what the person added and how the text was produced.

items.title: Limited utility of consumer wearable APIs for predicting substance use and craving, despite model personalization
items.abstract: Abstract We explored the feasibility of predicting, using individually-tailored artificial intelligence (AI) models, substance use and craving from Fitbit data collected in free-living conditions. Most substances examined acutely raise heart rate, and craving is known to often involve autonomic arousal. Because heart rate responds to stress, exertion, and substance use differently between individuals, we sought to study in an exploratory experiment whether individualized artificial intelligence (AI) models could learn person-specific patterns that distinguish substance-related heart rate changes from other arousal when conditioned on current activity level. We also examined whether per-participant data coverage and participant adherence to the data collection protocol could explain gaps in performance. Sixteen participants contributed 47 participant–substance–task prediction scenarios (25 substance use, 22 craving) spanning six substances. For each scenario, we trained a model to predict ecological momentary assessment responses, comparing global supervised, global self-supervised, and personalized self-supervised modeling approaches. Discrimination was modest (mean AUROC 0.569–0.617) for all substances and for both craving and use prediction, and differences in data coverage and participant adherence did not explain performance gaps. These findings suggest that heart rate and step count from a consumer wristband carry limited substance-specific signal in isolation, and thus digital intervention research may gain more traction from targeting better-characterized antecedents such as stress than from predicting use or craving directly.

items.title: Lived Experiences of Senior High School English Teachers in Teaching Writing in the Advent of Generative AI Applications in Senior High Schools in San Mateo, Rizal
items.abstract: The study uncovered the dilemma of English Senior High School Teachers in teaching writing with the prevalence of using Generative AI. The study employed qualitative phenomenological research design to unravel the lived-experiences of the English teachers in Senior High Schools in San Mateo, Rizal. There were 8 participants who were interviewed through an in-depth interview to convey their personal perspectives on teaching writing in the advent of Generative AI. The emerging themes from the study are as follows: (1) Recognizing AI-Influenced through Familiarity and Inconsistency; (2) Navigating Uncertainty in Establishing Authenticity; (3) AI-Assistance and the Preservation of Student Writing; (4) Reconfiguring Writing Pedagogy and Assessment to Preserve Student Thinking; (5) Developing Teacher Preparedness through Experiences, Self-Learning and Professional Development; and (6) Reconstructing Academic Integrity through Ownership, Boundaries, and Transparency. The study revealed that the roles of the English teachers in teaching writing is diversified with the changing landscape of education and the integration of technology in teaching. English Senior High School Teachers reconciled the use of AI in teaching writing and look at AI tools that support learning. The participants in this study understood that the goal of technological advancements in schools in sustaining learning and successful integration of AI tools necessitates simultaneous advancement of technical skills, pedagogical flexibility, and the reconciliation of ethical judgement, while maintaining authenticity and academic integrity. The implications of this study support a context-driven and moderated use of AI in Senior High School Writing. Specific type of Generative AI used for writing, AI assisted writing, assessments using AI and integrity in AI-generated writing may be pursued in subsequent researches.

items.title: LLM-assisted dynamic graph reconfiguration for post-disaster compute-power collaborative resilience in energy-informatics systems
items.abstract: Extreme weather can jointly disrupt data-center, power-supply, and communication infrastructure, threatening the continuity of critical tasks through resource degradation and migration restrictions. Meanwhile, operating information is scattered across heterogeneous reports, alarms, and logs, making it difficult to use directly in computation. Migration candidates identified solely through network connectivity may also be infeasible because of insufficient computing, power, or communication support. To address these challenges, this paper proposes LA-NADGR, an LLM-assisted neighbor-aware dynamic graph reconfiguration framework. The framework first uses schema-guided LLM extraction to convert post-disaster information into evidence-linked engineering records. It then integrates monitored states with extracted information to construct a compute-power collaborative constraint graph. Finally, neighbor-survival perception, task-aware action masking, and candidate selection generate a task-oriented cooperation topology. By separating information extraction from action admission, the framework exploits the LLM’s ability to process heterogeneous information while using deterministic engineering constraints to prevent infeasible actions from entering the scheduling candidate space. The framework is evaluated through structured-extraction, field-corruption robustness, and network-simulation experiments. On a controlled benchmark containing 50 samples, three local instruction models achieve field accuracies of 81.8%–96.0% and first-response schema validity rates of 77.5%–100% on 40 held-out test samples. Model-conditioned stress tests conducted over 20 fixed random seeds show that, at a 10% rate of missing or erroneous safety-critical fields, the pipeline with all three safeguards enabled achieves unsafe-admission rates of 0.96% and 6.74%, respectively. Ablation results further establish the contributions of evidence filtering, conservative imputation, and deterministic constraint checking. Under a severe regionally correlated failure scenario, LA-NADGR achieves both cross-node task reachability and a task-averaged feasible-candidate ratio of 68.4%. Its task deployment and success rates both reach 78.5%, improving task success by 3.2 percentage points over communication-only reconfiguration. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves the engineering feasibility of post-disaster cooperation candidates and supports critical-task deployment.

items.title: LLM-Based Policy Compliance Verification of Loan Applications
items.abstract: Banks rely on extensive internal policy frameworks to ensure that corporate lending decisions comply with regulatory requirements and internal risk standards. Reviewing loan applications against these policies is a largely manual and knowledge-intensive process, which can lead to overlooked policy violations or exceptions. This report presents a prototype of an LLM-based policy checker that automatically verifies loan applications against internal lending policies. The proposed approach follows a two-step architecture. First, compliance-relevant rules are automatically extracted from policy documents and converted into structured, machine-readable representations. Second, loan applications are evaluated against the extracted rules to identify policy exceptions, non-compliant findings, missing information, and cases requiring manual review. Evaluation results demonstrate that the rule extraction process is highly stable across multiple runs and consistently captures rules identified as critical by a domain expert. When evaluated on 11 real loan applications with known policy exceptions, the system successfully detected the majority of these exceptions and identified additional compliance issues that had previously been overlooked during manual reviews. While the approach produces false positives and cannot fully replace human judgement, the results indicate that LLM-based policy compliance verification can provide valuable support in the loan application verification process by highlighting potential compliance risks.

items.title: LLM-Driven User Preference Topic Modeling for Design Decision Support
items.abstract: Online reviews of home medical devices are noisy, heterogeneous, and uneven in information density, which makes it hard to turn the voice of the customer into engineering design decisions. This study proposes and validates a review-mining framework that couples rule-based data governance with a locally deployed large language model (LLM) and complex-network analysis. Taking home oxygen concentrators as the case, we collected 25,893 raw review entries from JD.com, Taobao, and Tmall. Because overlapping collection windows made 80.4% of these rows redundant (5084 unique review texts), a four-stage pipeline combining regular-expression cleaning, domain-relevance filtering, low-value review removal, and exact-plus-prefix deduplication refined them into a 2238-review corpus (44.0% of the unique review texts). A locally hosted Qwen3-8B model then performed aspect-level extraction within nine predefined design aspects, yielding 6068 structured aspect–topic–confidence records from 2214 reviews (98.9% parsing success), and scored sentiment for 6052 unique review–aspect pairs on a [−1, 1] scale. From these records, we built a topic co-occurrence network (202 nodes and 1895 edges after low-frequency filtering) and ranked design requirements with a Composite Centrality Index (CCI; weights 0.4/0.4/0.2 over min–max-normalized degree, betweenness, and closeness). Simple Operation (CCI = 1.000) and Low Noise (0.981) dominate user preference, followed by Solid Build Quality (0.611) and Oxygen Concentration (0.574); sentiment is strongly polarized on acoustic experience (Low Noise +0.755 vs. Excessive Noise −0.560). Five checks support these findings: an LDA baseline produced substantially coarser, partly brand-dominated topics; the CCI ranking is stable under five alternative weightings (Spearman’s ρ ≥ 0.978) and across 16 combinations of network-construction thresholds; bootstrap resampling (B = 1000) places the top two topics within ranks 1–2 with 95% confidence; the leading themes replicate in a JD.com-only subnetwork; and manual validation of a stratified 450-pair sample (two blinded annotators, adjudicated gold standard) gave 87.6% aspect accuracy and 94.4% sentiment-polarity accuracy. The framework converts unstructured reviews into a quantified, traceable design-priority list for oxygen concentrator development; we interpret the resulting associations as descriptive evidence for prioritization, not as causal effects.

items.title: LLM-Orchestrated Evasion of Tabular NIDS and GAN Augmentation for Multimodal Detection
items.abstract: Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDSs) based on machine learning have demonstrated strong performance against known attack patterns. However, their robustness against adaptive evasion strategies orchestrated by modern Large Language Models (LLMs) remains largely unexplored. This study presents a reproducible framework for evaluating traffic-space evasion of a tabular network intrusion detection baseline by an instruction-constrained open-weight LLM and separately examines the effect of GAN-based augmentation on a multimodal detector’s clean-traffic performance. The proposed methodology employs an open-weight language model, constrained at the prompt and decoding levels to a bounded action space of protocol-legal transformations, to generate evasive variants of known attacks that are realized as network traffic. Two defensive configurations are compared on clean traffic using detection rate, F1-score, AUC-ROC, and false-positive rate, while evasion success rate is measured against the tabular baseline. Across five training seeds per configuration, GAN-based enrichment produced no detectable improvement in the multimodal detector, with differences between configurations being several times smaller than the variation across training seeds. Synthetic flows inherit their payload and packet-sequence modalities from real donor flows, so the augmentation acts on the flow-statistics branch alone. An adversary given repeated rounds of score feedback achieved no evasion of the tabular baseline under Configuration (i), the only configuration attacked, across any seed attack and did not outperform a random-mutation attacker operating over the same action space and query budget. All results are obtained on a single dataset, CIC-IDS2017, with sixteen seed attacks and five implemented transformation operators, where the conclusions are stated within those limits. These findings show that apparent gains from synthetic augmentation may be dominated by training variability and that LLM-guided search does not necessarily provide an advantage over simpler search strategies within a bounded, protocol-legal transformation space.

items.abstract: Penelitian ini menyajikan eksperimen penulisan jarak jauh untuk menganalisis secara komparatif representasi kota Makassar dalam dua korpus sastra yang berbeda: karya yang ditulis oleh manusia dan teks yang dihasilkan oleh Kecerdasan Buatan (AI). Maraknya penggunaan AI dalam produksi kreatif memicu pertanyaan epistemologis mendasar mengenai kepengarangan dan kapasitas mesin untuk menggambarkan entitas budaya. Makassar, dengan karakteristik sosio-spasialnya yang unik, berfungsi sebagai studi kasus untuk menguji perbedaan antara representasi yang didorong oleh pengalaman manusia dan yang berasal dari algoritma.Dengan memanfaatkan Large Language Models (LLMs) seperti ChatGPT menggunakan perintah yang identik dan dirancang dengan cermat, penelitian ini akan mengumpulkan korpus AI untuk disandingkan secara langsung dan kritis dengan korpus sastra yang sudah ada yang ditulis oleh manusia.Dengan menerapkan analisis teks komputasi tingkat lanjut (pemodelan topik, stilometri, analisis sentimen/leksikal) bersamaan dengan pembacaan cermat (close reading) secara kualitatif, penelitian ini bertujuan untuk membedakan pola tematik, stilistik, dan linguistik yang unik di dalam masing-masing korpus. Temuan yang diantisipasi akan menjelaskan kemampuan dan keterbatasan generatif AI dalam memproduksi konten yang bernuansa budaya, mengungkap potensi bias dalam data pelatihan, dan berkontribusi secara substansial pada konsep kreativitas dan representasi urban digital yang terus berkembang, terutama di bidang Humaniora Digital dan estetika komputasional.

items.title: Machine Learning-Based Vulnerability Detection in AI-Generated Source Code: A Systematic Literature Review and Research Directions
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of Generative AI and Large Language Models (LLMs) has transformed software development, but AI-generated code may contain security vulnerabilities such as injection flaws, weak authentication, and unsafe API usage. Traditional rule-based and static-analysis techniques struggle with semantically diverse generated code. This paper presents a systematic literature review of Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), Graph Neural Network, Transformer, and LLM-based vulnerability detection, with emphasis on AI-generated source code. It compares approaches, datasets, and code representations, and examines challenges including data imbalance, false positives, limited AI-generated datasets, and explainability. A conceptual framework combining preprocessing, structural and semantic representation, ML/DL classification, CWE categorization, explainability, and validation is proposed. Future directions include hybrid ML-LLM models, real-time IDE integration, and automated vulnerability repair..

items.title: Make or buy AI? Evidence on AI sourcing decisions and workforce outcomes
items.abstract: We examine how firms acquire artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities and how their AI sourcing decisions relate to workforce outcomes. Using Swedish enterprise surveys from 2019 and 2021 linked to financial statements and employer–employee data, we directly observe whether firms adopt AI and whether they outsource AI-related activities. AI adoption is concentrated among larger firms. Among adopters, pre-existing cost pressure is associated with outsourcing. Relative to non-adopters, both in-house adopters and outsourcers have higher subsequent employment and persistently higher shares of university-educated and computer-science (CS)-educated workers, with no further change in workforce composition in the year after adoption. Workforce outcomes are statistically indistinguishable between in-house adopters and outsourcers.

items.title: Manacá-1B-Instruct-2: Reproducible Safety Alignment for a Native Brazilian-Portuguese LLM. Negative DPO Results, a Controlled Composition Scan, and a Silent Failure Mode of the LLM Judge
items.abstract: Brazilian Portuguese remains underserved by open-source language models, and the few that are safety-aligned rarely document what did not work or validate comparisons with statistical significance. We present Manacá-1B-Instruct-2, the second-generation post-training alignment of Manacá-1B (1.72B parameters, trained from scratch for PT-BR), with an SFT corpus of 291,223 examples. We document three DPO attempts, all negative, including a case where the training reward margin reaches 1.0 while free generation does not change at all, and show that safety came from a dedicated safety-SFT (LLM-jp AnswerCarefully style), refined over three iterations until closing the safety-helpfulness frontier. A controlled scan of the fraction of general data in the safety-SFT mix (10% to 60%) reveals a non-monotonic over-refusal curve with a knee point at 40-50%. The final model is compared against four external PT-BR models on the same items, with Wilson confidence intervals and paired McNemar tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction: the lower bound of its safety interval (94.1%) lies above the upper bound of all four baselines. We also report a methodological finding for LLM-judge evaluation: on two of six safety items in MT-Bench-PT, the judge categorically refuses to assign a score regardless of the evaluated response, silently reducing the effective N of that category in every prior report of the project. We complement this with an n-gram decontamination check and a Chinchilla-anchored compute-budget table that attributes the gap in general capability to pre-training scale rather than alignment methodology. All code, raw data, logs, and scripts that produce every reported number are publicly released.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

items.title: Mapping Digital and Experiential Project-Based Learning in STEM Education: A Scientometric Analysis of Curriculum, Engagement and Research Fronts
items.abstract: Digital and experiential project-based learning (PBL) has become a prominent response to the demand for authentic, technology-mediated STEM instruction, yet existing bibliometric mappings of this literature have been confined to a single database, a single educational level or a window shorter than a decade. This study reports a scientometric analysis of the field for 2015-2024. A five-facet Boolean query was executed in Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection in April 2025. After removal of ineligible document types (n = 230) and cross-database duplicates (n = 666), 2,103 records were analysed in ScientoPy 2.1.3 using total output, average growth rate (AGR), average documents per year (ADY) and percentage of documents published in the last years (PDLY). Journal articles (n = 930) and conference papers (n = 757) dominated; review articles, although few (n = 68), showed the highest recency (PDLY = 25.0%), signalling a field entering consolidation. Author keywords concentrated on “project-based learning” (n = 307), “experiential learning” (n = 221) and “virtual reality” (n = 129), while “online learning” declined (AGR = −2), consistent with terminological migration. The United States led absolute output (n = 594), but Indonesia (PDLY = 44.8%) and India (PDLY = 30.3%) accelerated most steeply. Individual and institutional productivity was flat and unconcentrated: no author exceeded eight documents and no institution exceeded nine. The study contributes the first decade-scale, two-database performance and thematic map of digital PBL in STEM education and identifies assessment methodology, artificial-intelligence integration and cross-system comparative work as principal research fronts.

items.title: MARS - A foundational map auto-regressor
items.abstract: Map generation tasks feature extensive non-structural vectorized data (e.g., points, polylines, and polygons) and thus pose significant challenges to common pixel-wise generative models. Conventional approaches use multiple stages, first segmenting these features at the pixel level and then performing vectorized post-processing, with errors and complexity compounding at each stage. Motivated by the recent success of auto-regressive language modeling, we propose the first map foundation model, named Map Auto-Regressor (MARS), that is capable of generating both multi-polyline road networks and polygon buildings in a unified manner. For training MARS, we collected to our knowledge the largest multi-class map extraction dataset totaling 3.4M examples, which we call MAP-3M. Across four road and building datasets, MARS outperforms or matches the performance of multistage baselines. Additionally, we develop a "Chat with MARS" capability that enables interactive human-in-the-loop map generation and correction, supported by the auto-regressive nature of our end-to-end approach. We release our MAP-3M dataset and project demo page at (1) https://huggingface.co/datasets/bag-lab/MAP-3M and (2) https://huggingface.co/spaces/bag-lab/MARS, respectively.

items.title: Masculine honor, social visibility, and safety non-compliance: intentions and approval judgments in high-risk sectors in Turkey
items.abstract: Unsafe work in high-risk sectors cannot be explained only by knowledge deficits or weak safety management; workers may also attach reputational meaning to visible compliance. Drawing on honor theory and occupational-safety research on risk perception and social context, this study examined whether masculine honor values (hereafter honor values)—the belief that a man’s worth depends partly on a publicly defensible reputation—were associated with unsafe work intentions, lower perceived risk, and greater approval of safety-rule non-compliance among male workers in Turkish construction and shipbuilding. A worker survey (N = 244) was combined with a within-person vignette experiment in which the focal hazard was held constant while visibility was manipulated and audience identity and prior social comment varied orthogonally. Honor values were positively associated with unsafe work intentions (H1a) and approval of others’ violations (H1b), and negatively associated with perceived risk (H2). Perceived risk partially accounted for the honor–intention association (H3). The association between honor values and approval of non-compliance was stronger when the violation was public rather than private (H4), consistent with a reputational, visibility-contingent account. These findings identify a micro-level sociocultural pathway that complements knowledge- and risk-based accounts of safety decisions. They also suggest that safety communication and supervisory practice should address the social meaning of compliance, while the cross-sectional mediation and judgment-based vignette outcome limit causal and behavioral inference.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

items.title: MassNet: billion-scale AI-ready mass spectral corpus empowering scalable deep learning in proteomics
items.abstract: Here we present MassNet, inspired by large-scale data corpora of text and images; MassNet is an artificial intelligence (AI)-ready data corpus for mass spectrometry (MS)-based proteomics. The corpus contains 1.5 billion tandem MS spectra from high-quality data-dependent acquisition (DDA) MS data across 35 species. Approximately 1.7 million peptide precursors are from human samples. We further present an AI-ready DDA data format called Mass Spectrometry DDA Tensor (MSDT) for compact and standardized storage, curation and reuse of data from multiple sources, which can be optionally converted to a Lightning Memory-Mapped Database for accelerated input/output in deep learning. On the basis of MassNet, we develop XuanjiNovo, a nonautoregressive transformer model that leverages a curriculum learning strategy for de novo peptide sequencing. XuanjiNovo achieves 38.35–143.57% improvement over state-of-the-art methods on human Astral data. MassNet also supports additional downstream tasks, including retention time prediction and PSM rescoring. MassNet represents a foundational MS-based proteomics data resource, marking a critical milestone for AI proteomics research. This Article presents MassNet, a large-scale AI-ready corpus of 1.5 billion MS/MS spectra spanning 35 species, paired with a standardized storage format called Mass Spectrometry DDA Tensor (MSDT). Built on this resource, XuanjiNovo is a nonautoregressive transformer for de novo peptide sequencing that substantially outperforms previous methods.

items.title: Material and thermal properties of MgCl2 molten salt by ab initio and machine-learning molecular-dynamics simulations
items.abstract: We study the structural, thermophysical, and dynamical properties of molten MgCl2 over a wide temperature range using Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics (AIMD) and molecular dynamics simulations based on machine-learning interaction potentials (MLIPs). MLIPs can achieve near-AIMD accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost, enabling simulations of larger systems and longer timescales. This opens up the possibility of studying the system under out-of-equilibrium conditions, which in turn allows for the calculation of physical properties, such as the thermal conductivity or viscosity, that cannot be obtained reliably for the typical time and length scales accessible to AIMD. We follow two complementary approaches to develop and evaluate the MLIPs. First, we develop a Deep Potential (DP) from scratch using AIMD trajectories at different temperatures. Second, we also evaluate two out-of-the-box foundation models and a fine-tuned version of one of them. The fine-tuning is performed using configurations from the AIMD trajectories originally used to train the DP. We compare the predictions of the trained DP, the foundation models, and AIMD simulations with the available experimental data and provide a comprehensive calculation of the most important physical quantities of molten MgCl2. We compute densities, radial and angular distribution functions, thermal conductivity, heat capacity, viscosity, and diffusion coefficients over the 1000-1600 K temperature range. This range is relevant to important technological applications such as thermal energy storage, generation IV nuclear reactors, and concentrated solar power systems. Finally, we briefly review the accuracy and performance of the different MLIP versions used throughout the work.

items.title: MCAIR: Monitoring and Correcting Agent Unfaithfulness via Internal Representations
items.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in completing complex tasks through multi-step reasoning and tool interactions. However, recent studies have revealed that LLM-based agents can exhibit unfaithful behaviors, where their final reports fail to faithfully reflect their actual execution trajectories. Specifically, when agents fail to accomplish tasks through the intended sources or procedures, they may resort to alternative sources or strategies while failing to disclose such deviations, leading users to incorrectly believe that the tasks have been completed according to the original requirements. We refer to this specific form of agent unfaithfulness as Agent Completion Unfaithfulness. Detecting and mitigating agent completion unfaithfulness is critical yet remains largely unexplored. In this work, we propose MCAIR, a runtime monitoring and correction framework that leverages internal representations of LLM-based agents. MCAIR uses multi-step internal representations as inputs to train a risk-aware probe, enabling online detection of potential completion unfaithfulness during execution. Furthermore, MCAIR introduces a risk-guided correction loop that prompts agents to review their execution history and mitigate potential inconsistencies between their execution trajectories and final reports. Additionally, we construct ACUD, a dataset for Agent Completion Unfaithfulness detection that provides step-level execution traces, step-level internal representations, and consistency annotations for training and evaluating runtime detection probes. Experiments demonstrate that MCAIR outperforms LLM-as-a-judge baselines, generalizes across prompts and tasks, and effectively reduces agent completion unfaithfulness.

items.title: Measuring and Reducing Unusable Replies of LLM Agents
items.abstract: People delegate multi-step work to LLM agents and read only the reply that the agent hands back. Current evaluation scores task completion and the faithfulness of reports, and it leaves open whether the requester can understand and use the reply. We call this property reply usability and measure it with a reader model that takes the requester's position and tests whether the reply can be interpreted from what the requester has seen, is in the requester's language and answers the request. Its agreement with the majority of five annotators lies within the range of the individual annotators. Across eight models from seven families, 54% of 480 replies fail, and the best model still fails on 30%. Failed replies mostly point to material the requester has not seen or use labels that the agent coined during its work. Stating explicit requirements for the reply reduces the failure rate from 0.52 to 0.43 together with errors and omissions, and a secondary model that rewrites the reply reduces it to 0.36, which human annotators confirm in a blind comparison. Reply usability can thus be scored alongside task success and improved with one appended message or one call to a secondary model.

items.title: MEASURING STUDENTS' INFORMATION SECURITY COMPETENCE IN THE CONTEXT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: CRITERIA, INDICATORS AND RELIABILITY OF THE DIAGNOSTIC TOOLKIT
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education has created new opportunities for learning while increasing the complexity of information security risks faced by university students. These risks include phishing, identity theft, unauthorized disclosure of personal data, manipulated digital content, and the uncritical use of AI-generated information. Consequently, assessing students’ information security competence requires an approach that extends beyond theoretical knowledge and incorporates practical skills, risk assessment, responsible digital behaviour, and the critical evaluation of AI-generated outputs. This article proposes a multidimensional diagnostic assessment framework for measuring students’ information security competence in AI-supported educational environments. The framework comprises five criteria: cognitive, operational, analytical, behavioural, and ethical-legal. For each criterion, observable indicators and appropriate assessment methods are specified. The article also outlines procedures for evaluating the reliability and validity of the proposed diagnostic instruments, including internal consistency analysis, test–retest reliability, expert evaluation, and construct validation. The framework is informed by established digital competence and AI competence frameworks, as well as recognized principles of educational measurement. Since the proposed model has not been empirically validated within the scope of this article, its psychometric properties are presented as matters for future investigation rather than established findings. The proposed approach provides a methodological basis for developing evidence-based assessment instruments for higher education.

items.title: MEASURING THE GAP: A FOUR-BENCHMARK COMPARATIVE ASSESSMENT OF AI-DRIVEN BANKING FRAUD LAW IN INDIA, THE USA, AND THE UK
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has altered the way banks are defrauded, though not, in most jurisdictions, the legal text that governs it. This paper offers a comparative doctrinal analysis of the legal and regulatory framework for AI-driven banking fraud in India, the United States, and the United Kingdom against four benchmarks: coverage (whether legal definitions capture AI-specific fraud mechanisms), attributability (whether liability can be fixed on a human actor or institution when AI is involved), enforceability (whether investigative and supervisory tools can handle AI-mediated evidence), and proportionality (whether penalties and remedies match the harm AI-enabled fraud causes). Applying these benchmarks to primary law, regulatory instruments, and decided and pending case law, the paper finds that no jurisdiction scores strongly on all four. The United Kingdom leads on coverage and enforceability but is only partial on attributability and proportionality; the United States is strong on enforceability but unsettled on the other three; and India is weak on enforceability and proportionality while, like the United States, untested rather than deficient on coverage and attributability. The paper argues that the binary of a 'reactive' India against 'proactive' Western comparators is misleading: the three jurisdictions are converging on a sectoral, regulator-led model and differ chiefly in the institutional durability of their rule-making processes, not in the protectiveness of the rules those processes produce.

items.title: Medication Safety in the Era of Digital Health: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: Medication safety remains a major priority in contemporary healthcare systems because medication-related harm can occur across the entire medication-use process, including prescribing, dispensing, administration, monitoring, and patient self-management.Digital health technologies have created new opportunities to reduce preventable medication errors and improve pharmaceutical care.This comprehensive narrative review examines the role of electronic prescribing, computerized provider order entry, clinical decision support systems, artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence, digital pharmacovigilance, telepharmacy, mobile health applications, barcode medication administration, smart infusion pumps, automated dispensing systems, and closed-loop medication management in improving medication safety.The review also provides a critical appraisal of evidence, highlighting that many digital interventions reduce process-related errors, whereas fewer studies demonstrate consistent reductions in severe patient-centered outcomes.Digital medication safety is best understood as a sociotechnical process requiring pharmacist expertise, workflow integration, high-quality data, clinical governance, cybersecurity, patient engagement, and continuous evaluation.Pharmacists have a central role in validating prescriptions, optimizing alerts, interpreting artificial intelligence outputs, maintaining smart pump libraries, supporting telepharmacy, improving pharmacovigilance, and educating patients.Digital technologies can strengthen medication safety when they support, rather than replace, professional judgment and patient-centered care.

items.title: MemDuet: Learning Dual-Process Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
items.abstract: Reasoning over infinitely long documents is becoming a reality with recurrent memory agents. However, increasing context length exacerbates the trade-off between reasoning performance and inference efficiency. Inspired by Kahneman's account of fast and slow thinking, we propose MemDuet, a dual-process memory framework that learns to coordinate a small language model for fast, parallel evidence selection from raw context chunks (System 1) with a large language model for memory-update verification and memory updates in document order (System 2). We train MemDuet in three stages: supervised fine-tuning of System 1 for evidence selection, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) of System 2 for verification and memory rewriting, and joint optimization of both policies to coordinate selection and updating for long-context reasoning. Experiments on diverse long-context reasoning benchmarks (RULER-HQA, LongBench v2, and 2WikiMultiHopQA) demonstrate a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off as context length grows. Averaged across evaluation settings on the three datasets, MemDuet achieves an end-to-end inference speedup of 9.74x and an output-token reduction of 73.91% relative to RL-MemAgent.

items.title: Mission (Im)Possible: Towards Autonomous Discovery of Autopilot Logic Flaws in Open-Source Drone Frameworks
items.abstract: Autonomous drones are increasingly deployed in safety-critical tasks, yet their autopilot software can still contain subtle logic flaws that lead to unsafe behaviors. These flaws are difficult to discover with existing techniques because they often depend on semantic relationships across modules, commands, and runtime state, and rarely manifest as crashes or detectable failures. With recent advances in LLMs, we observe that, when equipped with essential domain knowledge and carefully crafted context, LLMs demonstrate strong capabilities in understanding the high-level semantics of autopilot systems, making them suitable for logic flaw discovery. However, LLMs are limited by their context and can be biased to the vulnerabilities frequently occurs in training dataset, while logic flaws often require higher-level semantic bug oracles to identify their existence. To bridge the gap, we present Impossible Mission Finder (IMF), a multi-agent system combining static analysis, dynamic execution and log analysis, that supports fully automated identify, test, and validate logic flaws in autonomous vehicles. IMF primarily contains three LLM agents, it first uses the auditor agent to propose logic flaw hypothesis based on carefully-crafted program slicing, then it launches tester agents to write and execute test cases for each candidate, and finally it spawns the log analyzer agent to validate the execution log against the flaw hypothesis. This enables IMF dynamically validate bug oracles in a case-by-case manner, making it suitable for discovering logic flaws that do not have a unified pattern. We evaluated IMF on two widely used open-source autopilot systems, PX4 and Ardupilot, leading to 105 previously unknown logic flaws, that can cause unsafe behaviors including mission interruption failures, invalid actions, entering into restricted fly zones etc.

items.title: Mitigating Video Hallucinations via Attention-Guided Representation Perturbation
items.abstract: Video large language models (Video LLMs) often generate responses unsupported by the input video. Contrastive decoding (CD) can mitigate these hallucinations, but its effectiveness depends on how the negative branch weakens visual evidence. Existing methods rely on predefined perturbations or masking guided by question reconstruction, offering limited control over the model's visual reliance during answer generation. We introduce Attention-guided Representation Perturbation for Contrastive Decoding (ARP-CD), a training-free framework for constructing contrastive negatives directly in representation space. ARP-CD uses the attention mass assigned to visual tokens at the answer-prediction position to guide bounded gradient updates of the language model's input visual hidden states. These updates reduce visual attention and produce a negative input, whose predictions are contrasted with those of the original branch throughout generation. Experiments across four Video LLMs and four benchmarks show that ARP-CD outperforms representative training-free baselines in most model--benchmark settings, reducing hallucinations while improving general video understanding. Further analyses show that attention-guided perturbation directions improve negative quality and that the resulting negatives provide effective contrastive references for correcting the original predictions.
